import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided by the user
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a clean aesthetic style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize relationships between key numerical and categorical features.
# - X-axis: Megapixels (resolution)
# - Y-axis: Price (USD)
# - Hue (color): Body Type (e.g., Mirrorless, DSLR, Compact)
# - Style (marker shape): Sensor Type (e.g., APS-C, Full Frame)
# - Size (marker size): Weight in grams (to show heavier cameras)
ax = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x="megapixels",
    y="price_usd",
    hue="body_type",
    style="sensor_type",
    size="weight_grams",
    sizes=(80, 500),  # Define the range for marker sizes
    palette="viridis",
    edgecolor='black', # Add an edge for better visibility of markers
    alpha=0.8
)

# Add text labels for each point to include brand and 4K video capability,
# which are useful for a small dataset to provide specific insights.
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    # Create a descriptive label for each camera
    video_status = "4K" if row['has_video_4k'] == 1 else "No 4K"
    label = f"{row['brand']} ({video_status})"
    
    # Position the text slightly offset from the marker
    ax.text(row['megapixels'] + 0.7, row['price_usd'] + 80, label,
            horizontalalignment='left', size='small', color='dimgray', weight='semibold')

# Add title and axis labels for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Body Type and Sensor Type', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to prevent overlap with data points or labels
plt.legend(title='Camera Attributes', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6) # Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.tight_layout() # Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig("output.png")
plt.close() # Close the plot to free up memory
